brief_title: Bioequivalence Study of Metformin Hydrochloride Extended-Release Tablets in Healthy Volunteers
official_title: A Single-Dose, Randomized, Open-Label, Two-Period, Two-Sequence Crossover Bioequivalence Study of Metformin Hydrochloride Extended-Release Tablets Under Fasting and Fed Conditions in Healthy Chinese Subjects

lead_sponsor.name: The Affiliated Hospital Of Guizhou Medical University

brief_summary:
Metformin is widely used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Its glucose-lowering effects involve suppression of hepatic glucose production and improvements in insulin sensitivity.

The purpose of this study was to evaluate the bioequivalence, pharmacokinetic characteristics, and safety of a test metformin hydrochloride extended-release tablet (1 g) compared with the reference formulation in healthy Chinese subjects under fasting and fed conditions.

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Healthy Chinese male or female subjects aged ≥18 years;
* Body weight ≥50 kg for males and ≥45 kg for females, with a body mass index (BMI) of 19.0-26.0 kg/m² (inclusive), calculated as body weight (kg) divided by height squared (m²);
* Subjects who were able to understand and comply with the study procedures, voluntarily agreed to participate in the study, and provided written informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Subjects with a history or presence of diseases considered clinically significant by the investigator, including but not limited to disorders of the cardiovascular, digestive, genitourinary, respiratory, hematological, endocrine, immune, neuropsychiatric, or musculoskeletal systems. Particular attention was given to gastrointestinal dysfunction (such as diarrhea or constipation), peptic ulcers, gastrointestinal surgery, or other conditions that might affect drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion.
* Subjects with clinically significant abnormalities identified by the investigator during physical examination, vital sign assessment, laboratory tests, 12-lead electrocardiography (ECG), or frontal chest X-ray examination.
* Subjects with a history of hypoglycemia.
* Subjects who had undergone surgery within 3 months before screening, planned to undergo surgery during the study, or had previously undergone any surgical procedure that could affect drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, or excretion.
* Subjects prone to nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea, or who had experienced severe vomiting or diarrhea within 1 week before screening.
* Subjects with a history of clinically significant food or drug allergies, as determined by the investigator; known hypersensitivity to metformin or any of its excipients; or a history of allergic disorders, including asthma, urticaria, or eczematous dermatitis.
* Subjects with positive test results for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg), hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibodies, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), or Treponema pallidum antibodies (TP-Ab).
* Subjects with a history of drug abuse within 12 months before screening or a positive urine drug screening result.
* Subjects who regularly consumed alcohol within 6 months before screening, defined as an average consumption of more than 14 units of alcohol per week (1 unit ≈ 285 mL of beer containing 3.5% alcohol, 25 mL of spirits containing 40% alcohol, or 85 mL of wine containing 12% alcohol); who were unable to abstain from alcohol from 48 hours before dosing throughout the study; or who had a positive breath alcohol test.
* Subjects who smoked an average of ≥5 cigarettes per day within 3 months before screening or were unable to abstain from smoking from 48 hours before the first dose until the end of the study.
* Subjects who had received any blood transfusion or blood products within 3 months before screening or had experienced blood loss of ≥400 mL due to other causes, excluding physiological menstrual blood loss in female subjects.
* Subjects who had participated in another clinical trial within 3 months before screening.
* Subjects who had used any prescription medications, over-the-counter medications, traditional Chinese medicines, or health supplements within 4 weeks before screening.
* Subjects who had received any vaccination within 4 weeks before screening or planned to receive a vaccination during the study.
* Subjects with special dietary requirements or who were unable to comply with the prescribed diet and related restrictions (e.g., intolerance to the standardized meal or high-fat meal); or who had consumed xanthine- or caffeine-rich beverages or foods (such as coffee, tea, cola, chocolate, or animal liver), certain fruits or fruit juices that might affect drug metabolism (such as grapefruit, pomelo, mango, or dragon fruit), or alcohol-containing foods or beverages within 48 hours before administration of the investigational product.
* Subjects with lactose or galactose intolerance.
* Female subjects who were pregnant or breastfeeding, or who had a positive pregnancy test before the study; male or female subjects who were unable or unwilling to use effective contraception approved by the investigator during the required study period; subjects who planned to donate sperm or ova from the time of signing the informed consent form until 3 months after the last dose; or female subjects who had engaged in sexual intercourse without effective contraception within 14 days before signing the informed consent form.
* Subjects who had difficulty swallowing tablets.
* Subjects who were unable to tolerate venipuncture or had a history of needle-related or blood-related syncope.
* Subjects considered unsuitable for participation in the study by the investigator or who voluntarily withdrew from the study for personal reasons.
